science.title: For the first time, scientists watch sound jump between quantum states
science.summary: Stanford researchers have recorded the first real-time quantum jumps of sound, watching single phonons abruptly vanish from one energy state to another. The breakthrough could open new paths for quantum computing, error correction, highly sensitive biological sensors, and next-generation sound-based devices.

science.title: Stanford scientists discover the human brain may actually be two separate organs
science.summary: Scientists have found that the human brain develops from two distinct cellular systems, suggesting that evolution fused together two ancient nervous systems with very different jobs. science.title: Scientists find that “perfect” systems may be surprisingly fragile
science.summary: Complex systems may work better when their parts are not perfectly alike. science.title: Brain scans reveal a possible cause of long COVID fatigue and brain fog
science.summary: Researchers have found evidence that long COVID may damage dopamine releasing neurons in the brain, potentially explaining persistent fatigue, low motivation, slowed movement, and memory difficulties. The discovery could lead to new treatments that target the brain's dopamine system.

science.title: Scientists discover first new penguin species in more than 100 years
science.summary: Genetic evidence has revealed a previously unknown gentoo penguin species on the remote Kerguelen Islands and shown that gentoos actually consist of four distinct species. The discovery also highlights a growing threat, as warming oceans could leave several island populations with little suitable habitat by 2050.

medicine.title: Weight loss alone does not explain lower heart disease risk for those on semaglutide
medicine.summary: Semaglutide is known to reduce the risk of serious heart disease. However, a new study published in the European Heart Journal suggests that this effect cannot be entirely explained by patients losing weight on the drug.

medicine.summary: A major analysis of 139 clinical trials involving nearly 10,000 people suggests that some of the simplest treatments may work best for knee osteoarthritis. medicine.title: Stopping Ozempic may raise heart attack and stroke risk
medicine.summary: A large study suggests the cardiovascular benefits of GLP-1 drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound can disappear surprisingly quickly when treatment stops. After two years off the medications, patients had a 22% higher risk of heart attack, stroke, and death compared with those who stayed on them.
